subject: Helix Labs commitment & pricing path — clarification on slab vs rate-card
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Wong <alice.wong@helixlabs.com>
Cc: contracts@helixlabs.com
Date: Sat, 12 Dec 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Helix Labs commitment & pricing path — clarification on slab vs rate-card

Hi Alice,

Thanks again for the time yesterday — good discussion. Per follow-up, I’m sharing two possible paths for Helix’s hosted API usage:

1) Standard Rate-card: pay-as-you-go per-token pricing (listed in our published rate card). Simple, no commit, scales with usage.
2) Commit Slab: a 12-month committed spend with blended per-token slabs (lower effective unit price above breakpoints) + optional ramp credits for Q1.

You mentioned procurement prefers a committed structure but they need clarity on how slab breakpoints interact with overage and early termination. I attached a draft SOW and a sample slab calculation spreadsheet so you can see the mechanics.

Can you confirm if procurement wants: (a) a strict committed spend with monthly true-ups, or (b) a flexible banding model where usage above the commit is billed at a higher slab rate but not prorated into prior months? If you prefer a call I can loop in Ben and Karthik from Commercial.

Next step: your preference + any required procurement terms (PO cadence, invoicing contact).

Best,

Hannah Schmitt
Account Executive, Americas
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Helix_SOW_v2.pdf (pdf)]
[Attachment: proposed-slab-pricing.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: Alice Wong <alice.wong@helixlabs.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.ai>
Cc: contracts@helixlabs.com
Date: Mon, 14 Dec 2026 10:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Helix Labs commitment & pricing path — clarification on slab vs rate-card

Hannah,

Thanks — this is helpful. Procurement leans toward a commit but with a couple of asks:
- They want overage protection: if we exceed the committed tokens in any month, it should bill at the next slab rate (no retroactive reallocation).
- They’ll request a 90‑day ramp (first three months capped at 50% of committed monthly tokens) with makegood credits applied at month 6 if we stay below.
- Need confirmation on security appendix and SOC 2 evidence (contracts@helixlabs.com is on this thread).

Can Ben/Karthik confirm if that overage approach and the 90‑day ramp are workable? Also, any room on the effective per-token price at the largest slab?

—Alice
Procurement Lead, Helix Labs

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 08:26:00 -08:00
Subject: Fwd: Helix Labs commitment & pricing path — escalation for slab exceptions

Looping you both in. Procurement wants the committed path with: overage billing at next slab (no retroactive rebanding), 90‑day ramp with makegood credits, and a request for a slight discount at the top slab. Helix looks like a mid‑market expansion account with high growth potential — likely >$1M ARR within 12 months if usage ramps.

I think we can move on a concession here but need pricing sign‑off. Proposed concession: reduce top slab effective per-token by 8% vs the rate‑card published price, with the following guardrails:
- Minimum 12‑month commitment at $650k ARR equivalent
- 90‑day ramp (first three months capped at 50% committed tokens) with makegood credits applied over months 4–6 if ramp misses targets
- No retroactive slab reallocation; overage billed at next slab as requested

Karthik — can you confirm margin impact and whether Finance will allow the 8% at that commit? If not, provide an alternative breakpoint we can present.

Ben
Director, Sales
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-ratecard-2026.pdf (pdf)]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 16 Dec 2026 13:40:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Helix Labs commitment & pricing path — margin & alternative

Ben/Hannah,

Reviewed — background numbers: at a $650k commit the blended gross margin holds around 46% before accounting for forecasting error and egress. An 8% cut at the top slab would push blended margin toward 39% if Helix skews heavily into high‑context generation (long sequences). That’s getting tight.

Two alternatives that keep revenue and give the customer perceived value:
1) Hybrid concession: 5% top‑slab discount + 2 months of ramp credits (instead of credits spread over 3 months), with a performance clause that restores standard rate if usage >2x forecast for three consecutive months.
2) Volume share model: keep rate‑card pricing but introduce a quarterly true‑up incentive where if Helix exceeds forecast by >30% quarter over quarter, they earn a one‑time credit equal to 10% of overage that quarter (reward growth but protect margin).

Also, SOC 2 and security appendix are standard — send me the procurement checklist and I’ll confirm timelines for evidence.

Karthik
Head of Commercial Finance
Redwood Inference

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Wong <alice.wong@helixlabs.com>, contracts@helixlabs.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 18 Dec 2026 16:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Helix Labs commitment & pricing path — clarification on slab vs rate-card

Alice — thanks for the asks and procurement note. After internal review we can offer the hybrid concession (option 1 from Karthik):

- 12‑month committed spend (minimum $650k ARR equivalent)
- Top slab effective per‑token discount: 5% off published rate card (applies only after hitting the slab breakpoint)
- 90‑day ramp: first three months capped at 50% of committed monthly tokens; we’ll apply 2 months of ramp credits (applied as offset to months 4–5) rather than spreading them over three months
- Overages billed at the next slab with no retroactive reallocation
- Performance clause: if usage >2x forecast for three consecutive months, standard rate card reconvenes for subsequent months

I’ve attached an updated SOW and a sample slab calculator reflecting the 5% concession and the ramp credit mechanics. If this looks acceptable, we can escalate to legal for a short appendix to the MSA and get SOC 2 evidence over the next two weeks.

Next step: please confirm acceptance of the hybrid concession and we’ll open a DocuSign for the SOW.

Best,

Hannah Schmitt
Account Executive, Americas
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Helix_SOW_v2_annotated.pdf (pdf)]
